numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Index.get_indexer with method="pad", "backfill", or "nearest" returned incorrect indices when the target contained NaT or NaN values; for pad, searchsorted places NaT at the end so searchsorted(...) - 1 returned the last valid index instead of -1. numerical_characteristics.dtype: The defect was reported for a tz-aware DatetimeIndex (datetime64[ns, US/Central]) target-index dtype mismatch, which caused object-dtype conversion and a TypeError on the nearest path. The passages also name float64 Index with NaN and TimedeltaIndex with NaT as affected. No passage states a dtype where the defect is absent, so the one-dtype-versus-another contrast is not established.
category_specific_evidence: Special values involved are NaN (float64 Index target) and NaT (DatetimeIndex and TimedeltaIndex targets); expected handling is to return -1 for method pad, backfill, or nearest.
NaN in a float64 Index target with method pad/backfill/nearest must yield -1 (test_get_indexer_nan_target, GH#32572, expected np.array([-1], dtype=np.intp)).
NaT in a TimedeltaIndex target with method pad/backfill/nearest must yield -1 (test_get_indexer_nat_target, GH#32572).
Root cause: searchsorted places NaT at the end of the array, so for pad searchsorted(...) - 1 returned the last valid index instead of -1 (PR#64796).
Fix location: in _get_indexer, when method is not None and target._can_hold_na and not target._is_multi, set indexer[target._isnan] = -1 (pandas/core/indexes/base.py diff).
Issue report: DatetimeIndex with tz=US/Central and target DatetimeIndex([pd.NaT]); get_indexer(method='nearest') returned 1301 while the default method returned -1 (issue#32572).

Issue #32572 says the tz-aware DatetimeIndex is converted to object dtype on the path where dtype differs from the target (datetime64[ns, tz] vs datetime64[ns]), causing the 'cannot subtract ndarray' error.
Passages do not mention +/-inf, signed zero, or subnormal values; those special-value categories are not evidenced.
